title: Understanding One-Hot Encoding
text: When you one-hot encode a categorical variable, you create a new binary column for each category. For example, if you one-hot encode the 'sex' column, you will create two new columns: one for 'male' and one for 'female'.

title: Columns in the Design Matrix
text: The design matrix \( \Phi_2 \) includes one-hot encoded columns for 'sex' and $$'embark_{town'}$$, as well as an intercept term. How many columns does this result in?

title: Counting One-Hot Encoded Columns
text: The 'sex' column has $$2$$ categories, and the $$'embark_{town'}$$ column has $$5$$ categories. How many one-hot encoded columns will these produce?

title: Calculating Total Columns
text: Calculate the total number of columns in \( \Phi_2 \) by adding the number of one-hot encoded columns and the intercept term.

title: Full Column Rank
text: A matrix is full column rank if all its columns are linearly independent. Consider if the columns in \( \Phi_2 \) are linearly independent.

title: Checking Linear Independence
text: Are there any columns in \( \Phi_2 \) that can be expressed as a linear combination of other columns?
